reflection.text:
Unblinded as cytochalasin B, an actin disruptor, my call of Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.70 then p=0.48 was wrong. I correctly detected a cytokinesis-failure signal - reduced density and frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4 at 1 uM - but misattributed it to stabilized microtubules and mitotic failure rather than actin-ring failure described for cytochalasin B (PMID 5044763).

What misled me was the extreme tubulin brightening at 10 uM (tub_mean z=+27.7, tub_std z=+23.0) plus act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0, which I read as bundled polymer in e4. I discounted the review's correct warning: cell_area z=-8.4 at 1 uM and z=-12.1 at 10 uM meant shrinkage/compaction could explain brightening in both channels, and compare_to_reference_atlas e5 had 0/10 stabilizer neighbours versus Protein synthesis 5/10 and Cholesterol-lowering/Eg5. I then claimed rising with dose when both dose_response calls e6/e7 explicitly returned no estimable trend from 2 single-replicate wells.

The acquisition choice was decisive: only two wells acquired, each rep 1, with no low-dose actin-focused check and no stabilizer-versus-actin discriminator. I left Actin disruptors at 0.01-0.02 despite the large actin texture signal and multinucleation, anchoring on the first e4 stabilizer visual. Cytochalasins act by actin filament capping and cleaving (PMID 2916838) with acute effects on actin-binding protein function (PMID 40914162), so the actin channel change plus multinucleation should have promoted actin disruption, not tubulin stabilization.

Atlas comparison e5 correctly gave 0/10 microtubule-stabilizer neighbours, contradicting stabilizer call

Time-lapse studies show cytochalasin B blocks cytokinesis, producing binucleate/multinucleate cells.

reflection.next_experiment: Stain parallel plates with phalloidin for F-actin plus anti-tubulin and DNA at 0.1-1 uM cytochalasin B versus latrunculin A actin control and paclitaxel stabilizer control, with high-magnification imaging of cleavage furrows/contractile rings and washout live-imaging to show cytokinesis failure and multinucleation reversibility without stable microtubule bundles.
